**A later export must be redacted before it is stored so sensitive fields never become part of what is kept.**

That later export still carries values the store is not allowed to retain, such as identifiers, secrets, or other raw data. Writing it is what makes those values durable: they are then backed up, indexed, and returned on later reads. Redaction has to happen first so the only bytes saved are already safe to keep. Once the raw export is stored, those fields remain for as long as the stored object does.

**The twelve-second pause lets the new CSS finish landing on screen before the capture runs.**

A stylesheet edit is not visible in the same instant it is saved. The watcher has to see the file, the build has to emit the new CSS, the page has to load it, and layout, paint, fonts, and any transitions have to finish. Twelve seconds is a fixed cushion for that whole chain, so the capture is the settled frame and not a half-applied or mid-transition one.
